notes: The refresh rate setting no longer quietly caps the app at 60 Hz. "Max device refresh rate" used to ask Android for screen.refreshRate — and a WebView reports its own nominal rate (60), not the panel’s — so picking “max” on a 120 Hz phone pinned the whole app to 60 Hz for as long as it was open. Asking for an explicit rate is the only thing that requests one now, so “max” really is uncapped; a rate restored from an old backup that this screen cannot do falls back to the device rate instead of staying wrong

Pinning an artist in Discover can no longer take the app down. Everything the pin does after saving it is cosmetic, and a failure in any of it is now contained (the pin is kept, and the refresh failure is shown rather than thrown). Pinning also records itself in the flight recorder, so if the process ever does die in that path the next launch names it instead of leaving it to guesswork

Pinning several artists in a row no longer starts several artwork downloads and full-size image decodes at once. The backfill runs one artist at a time — the shape of that spike is what a crash right after pinning looks like on a phone that is also playing music

Updates never apply themselves on a background/foreground cycle any more. Opening the app from the widget, the notification, or the recent-apps list used to be able to hand over to a staged bundle for no reason. A staged update is now only handed over on a real app kill, or when you tap to install it from the update sheet
